name: tlib
description: Shared UI and utility library for FiveM resources

ignore.tests/lua/config-validate.lua: a tlib.config VALIDATOR fixture, not a config: its `licenseKey = 'abc123'` is a synthetic input proving a declared string key validates. The config rule matches it only because the basename contains `config`. Ignored by exact path rather than by widening the rule or by allowing `licenseKey` everywhere.

scripts.//secrets:check: Layer 3 of the credential gate, and the only layer that cannot be skipped: every credential-shaped key in every tracked config file must be BLANK at HEAD. The key set is derived from Diag.SECRET_PATTERNS in tLib (one list, parsed out of the Lua that the runtime redactor uses) rather than hand-listed -- a four-name array is exactly how Advanced.S3.AccessKey went uncovered. Layer 1 is .githooks/pre-commit, which refuses the commit; layer 2 blanks the staged copy of a release. The real value lives in the gitignored config.local.lua sidecar, so there is nothing to strip and nothing a `git pull` can overwrite. Exit 1 = a credential has a value; exit 2 = the gate could not run, which is NOT a pass.
scripts.//secrets:control: Negative control for the whole credential gate, end to end in a real git repository: a real `git init`, the real .githooks/pre-commit bytes, a real `git commit` and a real `git show HEAD:`, no stubs. Proves BOTH directions -- a planted credential-shaped key is refused at commit and at HEAD while the working tree keeps its value, and a blank config with a gitignored sidecar passes -- and then runs a BROKEN-GATE DRILL: the same planted credential with the pattern list narrowed so it cannot match MUST go green, without which a red verdict is not evidence the rule caused it. Also runs the Lua overlay suite with SECRETS_CONTROL=1, which deletes the sidecar and requires all 8 apply-assertions to flip.
scripts.secrets:control: bun run scripts/secret-gate-control.ts && SECRETS_CONTROL=1 bunx --bun --package fengari-node-cli fengari scripts/run-lua-suite.lua tests/lua/secrets-overlay.lua
scripts.//secrets:provision: Writes (or with --check asserts) the per-resource secret-gate wiring in all 11 sibling resources: .githooks/pre-commit, the four secrets:* package scripts, the config.local.lua .gitignore lines and .gitea/workflows/secrets.yml. Four small things times eleven repos is forty-four chances for one to be the stale one, and a stale gate is silent. Only tLib can see every sibling, so the --check belongs in tLib verify and nowhere else.
scripts.setup: bun run secrets:install-hooks && bun install && cd client/web && bun install
scripts.//docs:check: Validates docs/ before the sync workflow publishes it. The site CI only runs after that push has landed, so a bad page would already be live. Ported from tDB, plus one tLib-specific rule: a /docs link missing the group segment. The group-scoped link regex cannot see a bare /docs/<slug>, so four of them shipped here reading as zero findings.
scripts.//test:dom: tLib's DOM COMPONENT suite -- happy-dom + @solidjs/testing-library, which this package had NONE of until 2026-10-07. It runs from `client/web` and not from `tests/unit`, and that is resolution rather than preference: tLib is three bun install roots and only `client/web` has solid-js, so a test file under `tests/unit` cannot resolve it at all (node resolution walks up from the importing FILE; moving the script does not help). `client/web` is also the install the shipped bundle is built from, and its `resolve.dedupe` is reproduced in the preload -- without that a shared/ts component renders with NO OWNER, `onCleanup` never fires, and the page-wide escape/undo registries fill with scopes from earlier test files while every suite stays green. ⚠️ `--conditions=browser` is load-bearing and is set here because bunfig.toml has no equivalent key: without it solid-js resolves to its SSR build, where a component test throws and a bare reactivity test passes VACUOUSLY. The preload refuses to run without it. The wrapper also asserts the test paths exist and holds the pass count above a floor, because `bun test <missing path>` can contribute zero and still exit 0.
scripts.//test:dom:control: Negative control for the DOM suite. Seven defects, each planted in the REAL source bytes in memory through the loader (nothing is written to disk -- other agents work in this tree), each declaring the code PATH it travels, the EXACT tests it must redden and its measured total blast radius. Plus a BROKEN-GATE DRILL whose substitution cannot match, which MUST refuse to run -- without it, `every defect reddened something` is not evidence the patcher fired at all -- and a green-baseline check, without which no red result is attributable. ⚠️ A passing control proves the assertions still FIRE; it does not prove the rule set is complete, and it does not prove an assertion covers the path where the defect would really occur. It has already earned that distinction twice: `undo-depth-zero` originally exited 0, because the only nesting test registered the host scope FIRST and the equal-depth tie-break kept the editor winning for the wrong reason, so a `depth: 0` editor passed; and two multi-line anchors matched nothing because PropEditor.tsx is CRLF while LayoutEditor.tsx is LF. The seventh, `spread-arity-verbatim`, is the one with a CASCADING blast radius -- 54 of 81 tests, because the Solid 1 `spread` arity bug throws inside a render effect and Solid 2 halts the reactive graph for the whole PROCESS, so files that never import lucide-solid go red too.
scripts.//test:lua:control: Negative control for tests/lua/framerelay-election.lua, the two-client relay suite, and for tests/lua/runtimetxd-create-once.lua. Two planted defects, each of which must turn an EXACT named set of assertions red: `election` makes both clients report themselves the controller (planted in the real code path -- publishTick computes `mine` from tlib.occupancy.isController, so the module genuinely admits two writers on one statebag key, which is the pre-election bug replayed), and `clock` stops the world clock, the module's only notion of time and the one way a relay reasoned entirely about elapsed milliseconds can look perfect while measuring nothing. The runtimetxd half plants its two defects (`nocache`, `notag`) in the MODULE'S OWN SOURCE -- patched into the OS temp dir, since fengari ships no `io` -- and asserts each substitution matched exactly once, because a gsub that matched nothing hands the suite the unmodified module and the control then asserts that correct code is correct. Both runners also check each mode exits NON-ZERO with the control's own summary line rather than an unrelated crash, and that the suite is GREEN at baseline. THE THIRD RUNNER, scripts/primitives-control.ts, covers the three primitives ten resources are migrating onto -- tlib.permission's client mirror, tlib.net and tlib.opengate -- over SIX suites (net-guards, opengate, permission-onchange, permission-consumer, imports-autoload, imports-has) from one file -- the last of which is not a primitive but imports.lua's AUTOLOAD list, patched by the same machinery because its suite loads imports.lua by name the way the others dofile a module, and the failure it guards has no error in it at all: a consumer that declares nothing and never calls tlib.telemetry from Lua just never loads the module, so the NUI's flush lands on an unregistered callback and nothing transmits, because the whole value is the shared patcher and one drill over it. 19 defects, 24 suite runs. Each defect is planted in the MODULE'S OWN SOURCE, written with a copy of the suite into the OS temp dir (nothing is written to the tree -- other agents work in this tree), with that suite copy's one `dofile` of the module repointed at the patched file and its line count asserted unchanged. Each defect declares the code PATH it travels and the EXACT assertion that must redden -- a line number AND the assert's own message; these suites use plain `assert`, so the claim is the stronger `this is the FIRST assertion to fail`. Five defects redden two suites each. These suites print no control summary of their own, so the stand-in is that text and location, plus a NON-ZERO exit (fengari can print an unhandled Lua error and still exit zero) and the absence of the suite's success line. Two BROKEN-GATE DRILLS, one per anchor -- an unmatchable module anchor and a module the target suite does not load -- both of which MUST refuse the run, without which `every defect reddened something` is not evidence the patcher fired at all; and a green baseline for all five suites first, without which no red result is attributable. Proven to go red on two planted gate defects of its own: a no-op substitution, where find and replace are identical (1 of 19 red, `the suite exited 0 with a defect planted`), and an expectation moved to a neighbouring line (1 of 19 red, `expected the first failure to be ...`). ⚠️ A passing control proves the assertions still FIRE; it does not prove the rule set is complete, and it does not prove an assertion covers the path where the defect would really occur. Two measured limits of this one: the client source guard is asserted by ONE suite line covering six spoof values, so three separate defects there are distinguishable only by which value's message appears -- the 0-is-truthy case is never the first failure on its own -- and `broken-routed-to-denied` had to be planted as `do return ... end` because a bare `return` mid-block is a Lua syntax error, and a defect that cannot parse proves nothing about any assertion.
scripts.test:lua:control: bun run scripts/framerelay-control.ts && bun run scripts/runtimetxd-control.ts && bun run scripts/primitives-control.ts
scripts.typecheck:shared: cd shared/ts && bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json && bunx tsc --noEmit -p rage/tsconfig.json && bunx tsc --noEmit -p rage-viewer/tsconfig.json
scripts.//check:classes: Dispatches into client/web, which owns the uno.config.ts the check has to answer for. It was reachable only from inside that directory, so tLib was the one resource whose own `verify` never ran it -- and it now also carries the two CSS-contract gates (surface.css collisions, blurred box-shadow) that every consumer inherits through `runDeadClassCheck`.
scripts.//check:classes:control: Negative control for the two CSS-contract gates. Both are cheap to fool with a zero: walkCss returns [] for a directory that does not exist. Plants collisions and blurs in the OS temp dir and requires each to turn an EXACT NAMED SET red, requires a fixture of CORRECT usage (`.panel .toolbar`, a zero-blur shadow) to stay green, and runs a broken-gate drill that removes the rightmost-compound rule and requires the correct fixture to go red -- without which the green case proves nothing.
scripts.//check:comments: Comment-style gate, rules in docs/CODE-STYLE.md: no emoji in a comment, no box-drawing dividers, and no file of 200+ lines more than 30% whole-line comments. Reads the PUSHABLE set -- `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` -- not just what is committed, because the files about to go public are mostly not committed yet. String- and regex-aware in all three languages, which is the only judgement in it: server/sv_demo.lua prints a box-drawing banner and client strings carry warning glyphs, and a line-grep reads all of those as violations and gets the gate switched off. A trailing `// why` on a line of code does not count towards the ratio; only whole-line comments do. Licence- and copyright-headed files are skipped whole. The ratio rule carries scripts/comment-ratio-baseline.json, which is a RATCHET and not an allowlist: the files that were already over the ceiling are pinned at the count they had, a pinned file may only shrink, and the moment one is at or under the ceiling the gate demands its entry be DELETED -- so the ledger cannot outlive what it describes, which is exactly how a sibling resource's KNOWN_OPEN_FINDINGS came to claim five live bugs of which three were long fixed. `--write-baseline` regenerates it; do that only to record a deliberate new pin. Exit 1 = a finding; exit 2 = fewer than 300 files measured, i.e. the file set collapsed, which is NOT a pass.
scripts.//check:comments:control: Negative control for the comment-style gate. 29 cases over a fixture planted in the OS temp dir (nothing is written to the tree -- other agents work in this tree). Asserts the character classes against the glyphs the standard names AND against the typographic arrows, dashes and ellipsis it deliberately allows; the file-set floor in both directions; a planted emoji and a planted divider in each of .ts, .lua and .css, by file; both sides of both ratio thresholds, including that a file exactly AT the ceiling and a file of 199 lines are green -- that case caught a real off-by-one, since `split("\n").length` counts the trailing terminator as a line; that a trailing comment does not count; that a licence-headed file is exempt WITHOUT being merely unread, by requiring an identical file minus the licence to be red; and all four directions of the baseline RATCHET, including the two that demand an entry be deleted (a pinned file that fell under the ceiling, and a pinned file that is no longer measured at all). Then a broken-gate drill per rule through the real `skip` plumbing, and the drill that matters: a naive any-line-containing-the-character reader MUST go red on the correct fixture in all three languages, because the fixture carries a comment marker inside a string followed by decoration. No ratchet case hard-codes a count; each asks the gate for the fixture's own. Proven to go red on eight planted gate defects, each naming the exact cases it reddens: an unmatchable emoji class (2 of 29), an unmatchable box class (2 of 29), string tracking removed from the C-family scanner (2 of 29), the same removed from the Lua scanner (2 of 29), the floor set to 0 (1 of 29), and one per ratchet branch (1 of 29 each). The first version of the fixture could not see the string-tracking defects AT ALL until a comment-marker-inside-a-string line was added to it -- the measured case for why the drill is here and not just a passing assertion. A passing control proves the rules FIRE; it cannot judge whether a comment is worth keeping, which is a judgement docs/CODE-STYLE.md holds and no regex can.
scripts.//check:deadfiles: Orphan-file gate: a .ts/.tsx file that nothing imports and no entry point names. ⚠️ tLib is a PUBLISHED MIT library consumed by eleven resources here and by third parties outside this repo, so "no importer" is the normal case for a library file and can never be the verdict on its own. A knip/ts-prune-shaped answer flags the entire public API. The gate therefore reads four things that keep a file alive, in this order of authority: shared/ts/package.json's `exports` map (the DECLARED public surface -- ui/card, ui/color-picker, ui/meta, ui/progress and ui/tabs are each named there and imported by NOTHING anywhere in this estate, and a graph-only gate called all five dead); scripts/public-entries.json, the measured record of the deep paths consumers import by relative path OUTSIDE that map (115 of them -- build/*, fs/server, secrets/release, audio/wav, telemetry/*, every ui/* component); the import graph itself, through relative specifiers, `@tlib/shared/*` and `@/*`; and paths written as STRINGS rather than imported -- the ui_page html's module src and anything a package.json script hands to `bun`, which is the only thing keeping shared/ts/build/cef-output-contract-control.ts alive (tRadio runs it). `shared/ts/solid-compat/` is excluded because its files are reached by a `virtual:` specifier that exists only inside Vite, the same reason shared/ts/tsconfig.json excludes it. Exit 1 = an orphan; exit 2 = fewer than 250 files or fewer than 50 entry points, i.e. a set collapsed, which is NOT a pass.
scripts.//check:deadfiles:control: Negative control for the orphan-file gate. 16 checks over REAL git repositories created in the OS temp dir -- a real `git init`, because the gate gets its file set from `git ls-files` and a fixture that is not a repo would exercise a different path from the one that runs in anger. Nothing is written into the tree; other agents work in this tree. It plants one orphan and requires it to be REPORTED BY NAME, then requires that same orphan to go GREEN through each of the four readers in turn (the exports map, the recorded baseline, an import from a reachable file, a package.json script string) -- those four are the four ways a library file legitimately has no importer, and getting any one of them wrong is how an audit comes to recommend deleting a published API. A fixture of CORRECT shapes must stay green: a `.d.ts` and a `.test.ts` have no importer by their nature, and a gate that reports either is a gate that gets switched off. Both vacuity floors are asserted in the direction that matters -- a collapsed file set and a collapsed root set each exit 2, not 0. Then FIVE BROKEN-GATE DRILLS, one per reader: each reader is removed in turn and the fixture that was green BECAUSE of it MUST go red, without which "the exports map kept it alive" is an assertion about an exit code and nothing more. Proven to go red on three planted gate defects, each naming the set it reddens: the exports-map reader deleted (13 of 16 -- a CASCADING radius, because index.ts and pub.ts are the fixture's own roots), the orphan list hard-wired empty so the gate can never report anything (7 of 16), and the scripts/ entry glob narrowed to match nothing (3 of 16, including the real repo). ⚠️ A passing control proves the readers still FIRE. It does not prove the entry-point set is complete, and it cannot judge whether a file with no importer anywhere is a dead one or an unused public API -- that judgement belongs to whoever owns the published surface.
scripts.//check:boolattr: Solid 2 writes a boolean `true` attribute as the EMPTY string and REMOVES the attribute on `false`; Solid 1 stringified both. So every `[data-x="true"]` selector whose attribute is bound to a boolean in JSX went dead in the migration, silently -- no error, no lint finding, no failing test, just the base rule winning. That is what shipped tRadio's Callsign row with its Set button at half the row width and a label-height too high. Resolves how each attribute is actually PRODUCED before judging: a string ternary, a `String()`, a `dataset` write or static markup is CORRECT and is left alone, and React stringifies booleans so a React file is never a finding. Reports `unknown` and `never-emitted` without failing, because a gate that hard-fails on "I cannot prove this" gets routed around. Carries a per-attribute control fixture and requires BOTH readers (CSS selector and UnoCSS variant) to still find it -- deleting the variant reader left an earlier control at 7/7 and green. `--root <dir>` scans a consumer; a Solid 1 root reports `latent` and passes, and must NOT be pre-emptively converted, since presence matches the false state too while `false` still serialises to "false". Exit 1 = a dead selector; exit 2 = the control broke, which is NOT a pass.
scripts.//check:runtime-state: A release is installed by UNZIPPING IT OVER the live resource folder -- no installer, no merge, no prompt -- so one data.json in the archive replaces the owner's entire saved configuration in a single step, and data.json.bak cannot help because the replacement parses cleanly and every recovery path in this estate only fires on a file that does NOT parse. tRadio shipped one: every zone, codeplug, alert, tower, speaker, geo-zone, placed prop and tone mapping replaced, plus a real 274-character admin password handed to every customer. Asserts the FINISHED TREE, not the staging policy -- tELS's and tAFK's allowlists and tCAD's forbidden list are all policy, and the zip is built by walking the directory, so anything that writes into it after staging sails past them. Matched by BASENAME at any depth, with the pid/timestamp/version suffixes that cost tCAD a .gitignore line that MEASURABLY matched nothing. Second half checks tlib_modules against what tLib actually provides: a typo'd name is NOT a failed load, it is not a load at all -- imports.lua's eager loop raises nothing for a name that resolves to no file, and the first tlib.<name> is then an export proxy that throws "attempt to index a function value" wherever it happens to be used. The undeclared direction is deliberately absent and the module says why: lazy loading is legal, so only a FILE-SCOPE use is a bug, and deciding that needs a Lua parser rather than a regex. Exit 1 = a finding; exit 2 = the gate could not run, which is NOT a pass.
scripts.//check:runtime-state:control: Negative control for both halves. 28 checks: every forbidden name must turn an EXACT named rule red and no other, a fixture of LOOKALIKES (config.json, mydata.json, data.json5, data.jsonc, data-json.bak) must stay green because a gate that fails a release over config.json is a gate that gets a skip flag, and both vacuity floors must fire on an empty tree and on a directory with files but no fxmanifest. Then a BROKEN-GATE DRILL: each rule is removed in turn through the real `skip` plumbing and the fixture that was red MUST go green, without which a red verdict is not evidence the rule caused it. The tlib_modules half plants a typo'd name, a shared/imports directory with no loadable file in it, a declaration referenced ONLY inside a Lua comment (measured for real: every tlib.diag in tELS's cl_env.lua is in a comment), a commented-out declaration that must NOT be read as one, and a wrong tLib path -- which makes every declared name a ghost, so it must trip the floor instead of reporting nine confident lies. Proven to go red on two planted gate defects: a matcher narrowed to match nothing (4 of 28 red) and both floors removed (2 of 28 red).
scripts.//probe:jsonstore-real: Runs the REAL tlib.jsonstore seed/migrate path over the REAL data.json of every sibling that has one, because every document in tests/lua/jsonstore-schema.lua is synthetic and three keys wide while the files in this estate are 4 to 70 keys and up to 717 KB, with arrays 1700 entries long. Asserts the migration ran, that the pre-migration backup is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the file that was there, that every top-level key survived, that a deep sampled value is unchanged, and that the original was not modified. MEASURED: 7 real files pass, and all 7 go red when _backup is changed to a re-encode. NOT in check:regression: data.json is gitignored in every resource, so a fresh clone has none and the probe correctly exits 2 rather than passing on nothing. ⛔ It does NOT prove a migration is safe to run live -- cjson's own empty-table ambiguity is out of reach without a running FXServer, and the module says so.
scripts.//probe:focus: Proves the shared focus indicator PAINTS PIXELS, in the pinned Chromium 103, inside an overflow-hidden ancestor -- the geometry in which a ring's outward box-shadow is clipped to nothing. Reads each consumer's REAL built stylesheet and asserts every class string appears verbatim in the component source beside it, so it cannot drift into agreeing with itself. NOT in `verify`: it needs tELS, tAFK, tCAD, tUnit and tRadio/server built first, and `verify` does not build them -- and `shared/ts/build/nui-chromium.ts` is Windows-only (a `Win_x64` snapshot, `chrome-win/chrome.exe`, `powershell Expand-Archive`), so this is also the one script here that is not Linux-runnable. tUnit was added 2026-10-07: it was the one consumer NOT covered, which is exactly why two live `focus-visible:outline-ring` deletions shipped in it unnoticed. Two controls per case, each REQUIRED to paint 0 -- the box-shadow a ring compiles to, and the same outline at a positive offset.
scripts.//probe:preview: Where the marketplace preview's time actually goes, measured rather than reasoned about. Stage A times the exact string pipeline PreviewOverlay applies to a fetched document (the src|href rewrite, the centering-CSS and binder splices, parsePreviewCanvasSize) in bun; stage B times a real iframe load in the PINNED CHROMIUM 103 that CEF is, srcdoc vs a blob URL vs a second open with the frame destroyed between; stage C times the JSON encode/parse the document pays crossing into the NUI as a message field. The corpus is the REAL import set (backups/marketplace-import/manifest*.json, 21 documents, 91 KB to 12.9 MB) because the whole finding is their size distribution -- 91-99.8% of every one of them is base64 data: image payload inlined into the markup. --control re-measures each document with every data: URI replaced by a 1x1 GIF, which is what makes the verdict attributable rather than asserted: 5-7ms stripped against 47-103ms real, so 85-95% of the renderer cost IS the inlined images. It also has every frame REPORT ITSELF by postMessage (image count, decoded count, whether injected script ran, body width), since a sandboxed opaque-origin frame cannot be read from outside and a mode that rendered nothing would otherwise time as fast. NOT in verify or check:regression: shared/ts/build/nui-chromium.ts is Windows-only (a Win_x64 snapshot, chrome-win/chrome.exe, powershell Expand-Archive) and verify must run on Linux -- the same exemption as probe:focus -- and it reads a corpus outside this resource, so a fresh clone exits 2 (cannot run) rather than 0.
scripts.check:regression: bun run typecheck && bun run typecheck:shared && bun run typecheck:server && bun run check:imports && bun run check:classes && bun run check:classes:control && bun run check:boolattr && bun run check:runtime-state && bun run check:runtime-state:control && bun run check:deadfiles && bun run check:deadfiles:control && bun run check:comments && bun run check:comments:control && bun run secrets:provision:check && bun run secrets:control && bun run test && bun run test:dom && bun run test:dom:control && bun run test:lua && bun run test:lua:control
scripts.verify: bun run secrets:check && bun run lint && bun run check:regression && bun run build
